title: IODB: Stars and Bars
quickIdea: Identical objects into distinct boxes. Line the objects up as stars and separate the boxes with bars; the answer is the number of ways to place the bars.
remember: n identical objects into k distinct boxes, empty allowed: C(n+k-1, k-1).
Each box must get at least one: C(n-1, k-1).
Lower bound r per box: substitute yi = xi - r and use C(n-kr+k-1, k-1).
Upper bound: substitute or use inclusion-exclusion - stars and bars alone is not enough.
Five wordings, one template: multisets, non-negative integer solutions, non-decreasing sequences, combinations with repetition, distributing identical items.

example.prompt: x1 + x2 + x3 = 10 with each xi >= 0.

gateAngle: GATE CS 2003 Q.34 is the lower-bound form (answer C(m-kn+n-1, n-1)); GATE CS 2015 Set 3 Q.5 is the same template hidden inside 'non-decreasing digits' (15).

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many solutions does x1+x2+x3+x4 = 7 have with every xi >= 1?
variations.why: Give 1 to each variable (4 used), then distribute the remaining 3 freely: C(3+4-1, 3) = C(6,3) = 20.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many solutions does x1+x2+x3 = 6 have with 0 <= xi <= 2?
variations.why: Stars and bars alone gives C(8,2) = 28 and silently ignores the cap. With every coordinate at most 2 and three coordinates summing to 6, each coordinate must equal 2: the only solution is (2,2,2). A cap always needs a substitution or an inclusion-exclusion correction.

trap.what: Applying C(n+k-1, k-1) when the question has an upper bound or a strictly-positive condition.
trap.why: The plain formula allows any non-negative values. A cap or a lower bound changes the substitution, and caps usually need inclusion-exclusion.
trap.counterexample: x1+x2+x3 = 6 with each xi <= 2: stars and bars says 28, the truth is 1.

check.question: How many ways to distribute 5 identical sweets among 3 children, a child may get none?
